title: Multi-year margin lifecycle and hiring phasing (Q2 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet synthesizes: (1) a multi-year view of product-level gross margins under different pricing paths, (2) headcount/phasing plans tied to feature launches and capacity, and (3) an integrated sensitivity analysis showing how small price moves cascade to EBITDA and runway given hiring commitments.

Context / why this is needed:
- Sales momentum is outpacing initial capacity forecasts for Hosted API and Dedicated. We need a conservative, repeatable rubric to decide when to hire vs. when to shift pricing/commitment tiers.
- Ops lead time for GPU capacity and hiring is 4–6 months; decisions today affect Q3–Q4 throughput.
- Executive ask: call out breakpoints where a +3% price change offsets an incremental HC hire for the next 12 months.

Key assumptions (base case unless otherwise noted):
- ARR baseline (end of 2025): $78.4M.
- Revenue mix: Hosted API 55%, Dedicated 30%, Private/Enterprise 15%.
- Blended gross margin today: 42% (includes infra, cloud egress, model licensing, and support).
- Average ramp to productive for new eng hires: 5 months. New SRE/infra hires ramp slower (6 months).
- Average fully-loaded cost per new hire (across eng/pls/sre): $260k/year. Sales/customer success average fully-loaded: $210k/year.
- Unit economics sensitivity: each 1% price increase on Hosted API yields ~0.9% revenue uplift (elasticity ~0.9) in 12 months; Dedicated is relatively inelastic (+1% price -> +0.2% churn).
- Model cost compression roadmap: quantization + kernel improvements can reduce per-token variable cost by ~8% over next 9 months in a managed rollout.

High-level scenarios modeled (12-, 24-, 36-month outlooks):
1) Baseline: no price changes; hiring as previously planned (headcount plan v1).
2) Price tilt: Hosted API price +5% effective 2026-04-01, preserve hiring plan but delay two infra hires by one quarter.
3) Hiring-first: accelerate hiring (adds 18 HC in Q2–Q3 2026) to capture anticipated enterprise deals; no price change.
4) Conservative: price -5% (promotional), hiring freeze; focus on retention and automation.

Selected outputs (summaries from modeled spreadsheets):
- Baseline (12mo): ARR grows to $96M; gross margin edges to 44% due to model optimization; EBITDA margin +2ppt but runway unchanged.
- Price tilt +5%: ARR +$4.2M incremental in 12mo, gross margin +1.1ppt, net impact similar to delaying 2 infra hires (saves ~$130k run-rate in year 1).
- Hiring-first (18 HC): incremental opex +$4.5M FY run-rate; incremental revenue capture (from accelerated sales motion) +$6.2M ARR in 12mo; improves enterprise GTM capacity but reduces near-term EBITDA by ~1.6ppt.
- Conservative (promo -5%): ARR growth declines vs baseline by ~$3.0M, gross margin compresses 1.6ppt; short-term retention uptick unclear.

Break-even rules (operational heuristics derived from sensitivity):
- If expected incremental ARR per new sales/CSE hire < $600k ARR/year, prefer pricing increase or prioritizing automation over hiring.
- For infra/SRE hires: if capacity utilization by Dedicated customers < 72% projected after 3 months, delay hires and route requests via burst/spot capacity.
- If Hosted API elasticity signals sustained >10% volume decline after a price increase, revert within 60 days and trigger targeted discounts for top 10 accounts.

Headcount phasing (high level, quarter buckets):
- Q2 2026: +6 Sales/CSE (closed-won ramp), +4 Eng (runtime optimizations), +2 SRE (observability), +2 Finance/RevOps (billing automation) => total +14.
- Q3 2026: +6 Eng (dedicated infra), +4 Product (dedicated roadmap), +2 Legal/compliance => total +12.
- Q4 2026: contingent hires (0–8) depending on delta between ARR and modeled bookings-to-commitments.

Topline sensitivity matrix (excerpt):
- Hosted API price +1% -> +0.9% revenue (elasticity); gross margin +0.2–0.4ppt depending on mix.
- Hosted API price -1% -> -1.2% revenue over 6 months (promotional churn).
- Dedicated price +3% -> +0.6% immediate revenue (low churn); helps margin but risks renewal friction.

Sample calculation (illustrative):
- New Sales hire cost fully-loaded: $210k/year. If average ARR per rep = $900k with 40% gross margin on attributable revenue, contribution margin ~ $360k/year -> > break-even (rep is justified). Increasing price by 3% instead of hiring would have delivered ~ $27k incremental per $900k ARR (3% * 900k) — not sufficient to replace a top-performing rep.

Runway and runway sensitivity (finance view):
- Without any pricing changes and hiring as planned: runway to next funding trigger (internal threshold = 14 months) remains OK.
- With aggressive hiring (18 HC) and no price change: runway compresses to ~10 months unless we convert 60% of anticipated pipeline.
- Small price improvements (+3% blended) extend runway by ~0.6–1.4 months depending on elasticity assumptions.

Operational levers and tactical recommendations (actionable items):
- Short term (next 30 days): implement a limited +2% price experiment on new Hosted API customers (A/B test by region). Track net new revenue, churn, and top-account feedback. Responsible: Product + Pricing.
- Medium term (60–120 days): defer 2 infra hires if price experiment shows >+0.8% uplift without >3% churn. Put cost savings into reserved capacity commitments to lower variable cost. Responsible: Finance + Eng-Infra.
- Hiring policy update: require a 9–12 month payback analysis for all Sales & Customer Success hires and 12–18 months for infra/SRE hires.
- Trigger rules for rollback: immediate rollback within 60 days if any price experiment shows >5% increase in cancellation rate among top-quartile accounts.

Open questions / data needed (items to resolve before final):
- More granular ARR attribution by rep and cohort (need Sales ops export of ARR by rep, by month). TODO: Miguel to pull report by 2026-02-10.
- Confirm elasticity by region – we have only North America data; EMEA/APAC samples too small. TODO: Leah to coordinate localized A/B tests.
- Validate model optimization savings timeline with Applied ML (what fraction of 8% gets realized by Q3 vs Q4). TODO: Connor to sync with Applied ML 2026-02-05.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: price moves signal enterprise customers to renegotiate. Mitigation: roll price increases as feature/packaged changes (improved SLAs, dedicated support) rather than blunt list-price hikes.
- Risk: hiring early creates long-term fixed costs that outstrip realized revenue. Mitigation: use contingent offers with staggered start dates and bonus-linked milestones where possible.

Appendix (short tables inline)
- Example HC P&L (per-role annual fully-loaded):
  - Senior Engineer: $300k
  - Staff Engineer: $420k
  - SRE/Infra: $320k
  - Sales/CSE: $210k
  - Product/Design: $240k

- Scenario delta snapshot (12mo, rounded):
  - Baseline: ARR +$17.6M, EBITDA +1.8ppt
  - Price +5%: ARR +$21.8M, EBITDA +3.0ppt
  - Hiring-first (18 HC): ARR +$25.6M, EBITDA -1.6ppt (near-term)
  - Promo -5%: ARR +$14.6M, EBITDA -1.2ppt

Next steps / owner list:
- Miguel: pull ARR-by-rep export and pipeline conversion assumptions (due 2026-02-10).
- Leah: prepare region-split for A/B pricing experiment and regulatory notes for APAC (due 2026-02-12).
- Connor: confirm model cost compression schedule and provide gating milestones (due 2026-02-05).
- Aisha (owner): consolidate final scenario pack and send to Exec (target 2026-02-19).

Notes to self / rough ideas (scratchpad):
- Consider a small upsell SKU for Dedicated that bundles predictable throughput at a slight premium — could be a low-friction way to raise price without list-price changes.
- Evaluate whether we can push more customers into annual prepay discounts to smooth revenue and justify hiring.
- Can we run a high-touch onboarding program for top-20 Hosted API customers to reduce sensitivity to price moves?

Status: draft. This doc represents working hypotheses and an exportable sheet is attached in linked artifacts (JIRA/GH/Confluence ids above).
